...Now, Mr. Wittgenstein's view appears to envisage the alternatives:- (i) No atomic propositions are necessary (ii) No atomic propositions are contingent (iii) Some atomic propositions are necessary and others are contingent and to accept the first of these alternatives on the ground that each one of the atomic facts, the totalitv of which is the world, is contingent.' One might accordingly ask whether (i) is itself a contingent truth.
